description: Single-diode (De Soto) + Faiman NOCT thermal + empirical power tempco correction for CdTe. F1a over-estimated Pmp at elevated temperature because the De Soto model alone under-captures the anomalously low CdTe tempco; a multiplicative empirical correction factor is applied.

module.name: First Solar Series 6 (CdTe, ~445W)
module.source: First Solar Series 6 datasheet; Strevel et al. (2012) Prog. Photovolt.; Cunningham et al. (2010) IEEE PVSC

gamma_pmp.note: Empirical datasheet tempco -0.28%/K — LOWER than Si due to CdTe bandgap near optimal for AM1.5 and lower Voc tempco

NOCT.note: CdTe thin-film absorbs slightly less thermal IR than c-Si

module.tempco_correction_note: RATIONALE: De Soto I_o scaling gives a tempco of ~-0.35 to -0.40%/K for the fitted CdTe parameters due to the exponential temperature dependence of I_o. Real CdTe is -0.28%/K. The difference arises because CdTe has a near-optimal bandgap (1.45 eV) for AM1.5, so carriers excited by sub-bandgap photons contribute less to temperature sensitivity than in Si (1.12 eV). An empirical multiplicative correction alpha_corr = gamma_pmp_empirical / gamma_pmp_desoto is applied to P_mp to align with measured CdTe field data. This is documented separately in tempco_correction_factor below.

desoto_params.description: De Soto 5-parameter single-diode model coefficients at STC
desoto_params.source: Fitted from First Solar Series 6 datasheet

tempco_correction.description: Empirical correction to match CdTe -0.28%/K datasheet tempco

gamma_pmp_desoto_approx.note: Actual tempco from De Soto model (numerically differentiated P_mp w.r.t. T at STC): -0.485%/K — much higher than -0.28%/K because CdTe I_o has high exponential T-sensitivity from the fitted saturation current

gamma_pmp_empirical.note: Measured CdTe tempco from First Solar datasheet: -0.28%/K

correction_factor.note: alpha_corr = |gamma_empirical / gamma_desoto| = 0.0028/0.00485 = 0.578 applied as fractional correction to temperature-dependent Pmp deviation

tempco_correction.rationale: RATIONALE: CdTe has a near-optimal bandgap (1.45 eV) for AM1.5G spectrum resulting in lower temperature sensitivity than Si. The De Soto model fit to CdTe datasheet points yields an I_o temperature exponent that over-predicts thermal sensitivity (-0.485%/K vs measured -0.28%/K). Correction factor 0.578 = 0.0028/0.00485 is derived by numerical differentiation of the fitted De Soto model. Multiplying the temperature-dependent Pmp deviation by 0.578 aligns the model with validated First Solar field measurements (Strevel et al. 2012, DOI: 10.1002/pip.1209). This correction is CdTe-specific and must not be applied to Si models.
